newsitem.title: DENMARK: FEATURE - Santas sweat it out at World Summit.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Santas sweat it out at World Summit.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, July 22 - It's not the first time that politics have overshadowed the World Santa Congress.
The last time the row was over where "he" really lives. This year delegates are scrapping about just who is entitled to be a Father Christmas and whether they should move Christmas to the summer.

Before they even arrived in Copenhagen for this week's 34th congress, the 95 delegates had been upstaged by a breakaway group who held a rival gathering in the provincial town of Naestved south of the Danish capital.
"You are not a Father Christmas just because you wear a big white beard and a red robe," said Ole Lundsgaard, head of the Danish Santas Guild.
He said the hottest item on the agenda would be how to ensure that it is only genuine Father Christmases who children come to know.

"There is a grave danger that children's illusions could be ruined if a mass of fake Santas suddenly turn up on the Father Christmas circuit," said congress chairman Kurt Flemming, who doubles as a circus clown when his yuletide duties allow.
WHERE DOES HE REALLY LIVE
The Santa fraternity has been dogged in recent years over which Nordic country is Father Christmas's true home.
Greenland laid claim to the title, but Finnish Lapland, Sweden, Norway and Iceland all put in rival bids until agreeing to differ and concentrate on how best to do the job.

This week's programme requires Santas from Australia, Britain, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Scandinavia and the United States to stage yule shows, sample powerful Danish Christmas Ale and eat their way through a heavy traditional Christmas dinner at the height of the Danish summer.
The star of the show is 86-year-old Dayton C.Fouts from Arizona who is celebrating 60 years as Father Christmas.
Fouts will join the others in a grand Father Christmas parade through the centre of Copenhagen and take part in the Santa of the Year contest.
The conference agenda includes such thorny issues as better rooftop parking for Santa's sleigh and stronger ropes for roof elves.

"Modern children want bigger and better gifts like computers and cycles. Santas want to grant their wishes but these presents are so bulky that more reindeer and bigger sleighs are needed," Flemming told Reuters.
"Today there are satellite dishes on almost every roof so it is totally impossible for Santas to park extra-large sleighs with six reindeer on rooftops on Christmas Eve.
"We are lobbying politicians to stop the authorities from slapping huge rooftop parking fees on Santas during their yuletide rounds," Flemming said.
SAFETY FIRST
The drive for stronger ropes for the elves follows an accident last Christmas, when a rope lowering a Danish Santa snapped and he was badly hurt.
"The declining quality of Christmas rope is a major threat to Santas and roof elves," Flemming added.
"The Father Christmases will be discussing ways to get manufacturers to urgently improve rope quality."
In Denmark, where Christmas is celebrated on December 24, yule hobgoblins and elves -- play a prominent role along with Santa Claus -- known as 'yuleman' in Danish -- in seasonal festivities.
Because in most places Christmas is rarely ever truly white, the congress will also debate a proposal to move it to July 24 to make the festive season green.
"The vote on changing the date is going to be pretty close," Flemming said. "But I am confident that a majority of Santas will insist on keeping Christmas in December."
